entries.5ddb348d1f62f21e: Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥734,791 million, up 7.0% from the previous fiscal year. Revenue from external customers was largest for electricity and gas at ¥319,571 million, followed by telecommunications at ¥127,540 million, agency sales at ¥98,493 million, beverages at ¥85,314 million, finance at ¥45,526 million, insurance at ¥31,478 million and solutions at ¥26,866 million, in that order of size. In the revenue disaggregation table, of the ¥637,399 million of revenue recognized from contracts with customers, ¥528,102 million was 'continuing goods or services' (provided continuously every month) and ¥109,297 million was 'one-time goods or services' (provided when new contracts are concluded or at similar times). Separately, 'revenue recognized from other sources' of ¥97,391 million exists, including revenue under IFRS 9, IFRS 16, IFRS 17 and IAS 20. Of the ¥98,493 million in agency sales, ¥20,173 million is continuing and ¥78,320 million is one-time. On the expense side, sales commissions were ¥140,526 million (¥136,998 million in the previous fiscal year), and the securities report states that commissions based on sales volume are paid to sales agencies.

entries.7ba3b2b7739d2682: A business that sells and supplies electricity, gas and other products mainly to small and medium-sized enterprises and individuals. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥319,571 million (up 10.8% year on year) and operating profit was ¥35,848 million (up 1.1%), the largest revenue among the seven reportable segments. The securities report cites an increase in customer contracts, which raised stock profit that forms the basis of stable future earnings, as the reason. According to the securities report, stock profit is the profit obtained by deducting costs of retaining customers and the cost of services provided, among others, from the income received from basic contract charges, usage charges and insurance premiums paid monthly by customers after contracts are signed. In the securities report's status of affiliated companies, the consolidated subsidiaries whose main business is printed as 'Electricity and Gas' are Haruene Co., Ltd. and Stoene Co., Ltd., and both hold 100.0% of voting rights, all of it held indirectly (through a subsidiary of HIKARI TSUSHIN, INC.). Because Haruene's revenue (excluding internal revenue between consolidated companies) exceeds 10% of consolidated revenue, the securities report separately presents its major profit and loss information. As of March 31, 2026, the number of consolidated employees in this segment was 261 (with 72 temporary employees in addition).
entries.807ff1cb6955645f: A business that provides non-life insurance, life insurance, guarantee services and others, mainly to small and medium-sized enterprises and individuals. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥31,478 million (up 16.9% year on year) and operating profit was ¥9,368 million (up 14.0%). The securities report cites growth in customer contracts and an increase in stock profit as the reason. In the revenue disaggregation table, ¥25,235 million of this revenue is 'revenue recognized from other sources' and ¥6,243 million is revenue recognized from contracts with customers. The securities report explains that revenue recognized from other sources includes insurance revenue under IFRS No. 17, among other items. The individual table of affiliated companies in the securities report does not list any company whose main business is printed as 'Insurance'. The history section states that Sakura Non-Life Insurance Co., Ltd. obtained a non-life insurance business license in June 2019 and began full-scale insurance business. As of March 31, 2026, the number of consolidated employees in this segment was 184 (with 31 temporary employees in addition).

entries.a25ad2fb0a563f12: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥116,664 million, up 11.1% from the previous fiscal year. Segment profit, on an operating profit basis, was ¥35,848 million for electricity and gas, ¥29,383 million for telecommunications, ¥22,086 million for finance, ¥12,799 million for agency sales, ¥9,695 million for beverages, ¥9,368 million for insurance and ¥3,790 million for solutions (total for reportable segments ¥122,972 million; the reconciliation amount, including corporate expenses, was △¥6,307 million). The securities report cites, as the reason for the profits of electricity and gas, telecommunications and insurance, the growth in the number of customer contracts, which increased 'stock profit' (the profit remaining after deducting customer retention costs and service costs from the monthly fees and other payments received after contracts are signed). In addition to operating profit, there were finance income of ¥77,619 million (¥41,604 million in the previous fiscal year), finance costs of ¥22,399 million, share of profit or loss of investments accounted for using the equity method of ¥26,850 million (including a bargain purchase gain of ¥5,565 million arising when an equity-method affiliate was newly established), and other non-operating income and expenses of ¥346 million; profit before tax was ¥199,081 million (up 32.1% from the previous fiscal year), and profit attributable to owners of the parent was ¥151,014 million (up 28.5%). The breakdown of finance income includes dividends received of ¥28,938 million, foreign exchange gains of ¥21,304 million and interest income of ¥14,850 million, and the securities report explains the increase in profit before tax as due to increased finance income associated with the stronger dollar and an increase in share of profit of equity-method investments. The accounting standard is [[term:ifrs|IFRS]].

entries.a9a415555f55000a: The securities report sets 7 reportable segments: the 6 segments of electricity and gas, telecommunications, beverages, insurance, finance and solutions, which provide products and services planned and developed in-house, plus agency sales, which sells products of other companies. The contents are: sales and supply of electricity and gas; communication line services and related services; manufacture and home-delivery sales of natural mineral water; non-life insurance, life insurance and guarantee services; financial services such as microfinance; platforms such as customer management and payment management systems; and agency sales of various products of telecom carriers, manufacturers and others. The securities report's business risks section states that in the electricity business, the electricity sold to customers is mainly procured from the market.
entries.ae4e0fa6b74a9f80: A business that sells various products from telecommunications carriers, manufacturers and others on an agency basis, mainly to small and medium-sized enterprises and individuals. The securities report positions the other six reportable segments as 'provision of products and services planned and developed in-house', and this agency sales business as 'sales of other companies' products'. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥98,493 million (down 8.8% year on year). The securities report attributes this, among other things, to the transfer of shares in some consolidated subsidiaries in the previous fiscal year. Operating profit, by contrast, was ¥12,799 million (up 3.4%). The securities report explains this as being due, among other things, to recording a one-time gain from the sale of shares in some consolidated subsidiaries in the current fiscal year. In the securities report's status of affiliated companies, the consolidated subsidiaries whose main business is printed as 'Agency Sales' are [[company:ftgroup|FTGroup CO.,LTD.]] (72.6% of voting rights, of which 13.0% held indirectly), Members Mobile Co., Ltd., Telecom Service Co., Ltd. and J Communication Co., Ltd. The other three companies hold 100.0% of voting rights, all of it held indirectly. Its equity-method affiliates include [[company:bell-park|Bell-Park Co.,Ltd.]] (36.2% of voting rights, all held indirectly). The securities report's 'Material Contracts' section lists, as major agency contracts as of March 31, 2026, the contracts concluded by J Communication with KDDI, and by Telecom Service and Members Mobile with SoftBank, for outsourcing of mobile telephone service subscriptions and for the sale and purchase of mobile telephone terminals and related products. As of March 31, 2026, the number of consolidated employees in this segment was 142 (with 156 temporary employees in addition).

entries.f32b058cd5554100: A business that provides financial services such as microfinance, mainly to small and medium-sized enterprises and individuals. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥45,526 million (up 37.4% year on year) and operating profit was ¥22,086 million (up 23.6%). The securities report cites, among other reasons, that the business performed steadily. The year-on-year increase in revenue is the largest among the seven reportable segments. In the revenue disaggregation table, ¥42,047 million of this revenue is 'revenue recognized from other sources' and ¥3,479 million is revenue recognized from contracts with customers. The securities report explains that revenue recognized from other sources includes revenue under IFRS No. 9, lease revenue under IFRS No. 16, insurance revenue under IFRS No. 17, and government grants under IAS No. 20. 'Finance income' in the consolidated statement of income is a separate item from this segment's revenue. In the segment notes of the securities report, it is placed among the reconciling items that link segment profit to profit before tax. The individual table of affiliated companies in the securities report does not list any company whose main business is printed as 'Finance', and the securities report does not show whether such companies are included in 'Other 157 companies'. The history section states that the company began full-scale financial business overseas in May 2023. As of March 31, 2026, the number of consolidated employees in this segment was 1,311 (with 39 temporary employees in addition), the largest headcount among the seven reportable segments.
